Rashi on Shabbat 150b:10:1.hebrew: למיגז ליה גלימא - לתקן לו תכריכין, דאין היתר לדבר היום כלל:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:10:1.english: To cut a garment for him - To prepare shrouds for him, for there is no permissibility for this matter today at all.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:11:1.hebrew: ואע"ג דלא אבדיל - אסיפא דמתני' מתמה, דקתני ומביא פירות בידו — לקוצצן מן המחובר בלא הבדלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:11:1.english: Even though he has not recited Havdalah - [The Gemara] is expressing astonishment at the latter clause of the Mishnah, which teaches "and he brings produce in his hand" — [meaning] to cut them from what is attached [to the ground] without Havdalah.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:11:2.english: They taught [this] among the wine presses - For there is a cup [of wine] in the field.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:12:1.hebrew: המבדיל בין קודש לחול - להיכרא בעלמא, ללוות את המלך:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:12:1.english: The One who distinguishes between the sacred and the mundane - Merely as a sign, to escort the king [i.e., the departing Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:12:2.hebrew: ועבדינן צורכין - ואחר כך אנו מברכין על הכוס ברכה גמורה דהבדלה. וכ"ש דאי אבדיל בתפלה, מותר לעשות צרכיו וחוזר ומבדיל על הכוס:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:12:2.english: And we attend to our needs - And afterwards we recite the full blessing of Havdalah over the cup. And all the more so that if one recited Havdalah in [his] prayer, he is permitted to attend to his needs, and he again recites Havdalah over the cup.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:12:3.english: And we would cut wood - Chopping wood.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:13:1.english: To which - [does he] refer and establish [this] principle.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:13:2.hebrew: אי נימא ארישא - דקתני ת"ק לאיסורא, וקאתי אבא שאול לשוויה בה כללא. א"כ דכללא לאיסורא, ה"ל למימר בהדיא: "כל שאינו זכאי באמירה" — כגון אלו, שאינו רשאי לומר לחבירו "שכור לי פועלים" או "הבא לי פירות" למוצאי שבת — "אינו רשאי להחשיך" מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:13:2.english: If we say [it refers] to the first clause - Where the Tanna Kamma taught [a ruling] of prohibition, and Abba Shaul comes to establish a general principle regarding it: if so, that the general principle is [stated] for prohibition, he should have stated explicitly: "Anyone who is not entitled to speak [about it]" — such as these [cases], where one is not permitted to say to his fellow, "Hire workers for me" or "Bring produce for me" for after Shabbat — "he is not permitted to wait for nightfall," [is what] he should have [said].

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:1:1.hebrew: ושל מה בכך - כגון שכבר היו לצורך, אלא שעברו, כגון "כך וכך הוצאתי בבנין זה":
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:1:1.english: And [accounts] of: What [significance] does it have - For example, [expenses] that were already for a need, except that they have passed; for example, "Such and such [an amount] I spent on this building."

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:2:1.hebrew: חשבונות שעברו - לקמן מוקי לה דלא עברו לגמרי, שעדיין שכר הפועלים עליו שלא נתנו להן. ושל מה בכך — שעברו לגמרי ואין שכר פועלים עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:2:1.english: Calculations that have passed - Below, [the Gemara] establishes [this as referring to a case] where they have not completely passed, for the workers' wages are still [owed] by him, as he has not [yet] given [the wages] to them. And "[calculations] of what [consequence] is it" — [refers to a case] where they have completely passed, and no workers' wages are [owed] by him.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:2:2.english: I spent such and such - Thus, past [calculations] are permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:3:1.hebrew: תקשי לך היא גופא - ברייתא קמייתא: רישא קתני שעברו אסורין, וסיפא קתני של מה בכך מותרין, דהיינו עברו:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:3:1.english: It itself should be difficult for you - The first baraita: the first clause teaches [that calculations of] past [expenditures] are prohibited, and the latter clause teaches [that calculations] of no consequence are permitted, which is [the same as] past [expenditures].

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:4:1.hebrew: צלף - אילן גדול הוא ובעל ענפים הרבה, ושלשה מיני אוכל יש בפירותיו: אביונות, קפריסין, ולולבין:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:4:1.english: A caper bush - It is a large tree with many branches, and there are three types of food in its fruits: caperberries [aviyonot], caper buds [kafrisin], and young shoots [lulavin].

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:5:1.hebrew: שאם יש בורגנין - מע' אמה לע' אמה, הולך אפי' בשבת, שהכל חשוב כעיר אחת, וכל העיר כד' אמות, כדאמרינן בעירובין (דף כא.). וכיון דהוא דבר שיש לו היתר על ידי תקנה בשבת, מותר לאומרו אפילו במקום שאין שם ההיתר:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:5:1.english: For if there are guardhouses [burganin] - [Placed] from seventy cubits to seventy cubits [apart], one may walk [there] even on Shabbat, for the entire [area] is considered like a single city, and an entire city is [considered] like four cubits, as we say in Eruvin (21a). And since it is a matter that has a permitted way [to be done] through a provision on Shabbat, it is permitted to say it even in a place where that permitted [condition] is not present.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:6:1.hebrew: המחוברים - שא"א לקצצן בשבת ע"י שום תקנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:6:1.english: The attached [produce] - For it is impossible to cut them on Shabbat through any expedient.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:7:1.english: Straw - The ends of the ears of grain, [in Old French:] estrace.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:7:2.hebrew: בתיבנא סריא - שאפי' יש מחיצות, אינו מביא משום דמוקצה הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:7:2.english: With rotten straw - For even if there are partitions, one may not bring [it], because it is muktzeh.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:8:1.hebrew: על עסקי כלה ומת אין - דחפצי שמים הן, אבל על עסקי אחר, אפי' דומיא דכלה — לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:8:1.english: For the needs of a bride or a corpse, yes - Because they are matters of Heaven [mitzvah affairs]; but for the needs of another [person], even [needs] similar to [those of] a bride — no.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:9:1.hebrew: בשלמא אחר דומיא דכלה משכחת לה - דאסור להחשיך, כגון לחתוך מן המחובר:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:9:1.english: Granted, [for] another similar to a bride, you find it - That it is forbidden to wait until dark [at the Shabbat boundary], such as to cut from what is attached [to the ground].

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:9:2.english: To cut a myrtle [branch] for her - For they make a canopy of myrtle for the bride.

Rashi on Shabbat 150b:9:3.hebrew: אלא עסקי מת מאי היא - הבאה דארון ותכריכין. ואמאי לאחר לא? לימא הואיל ואם יש שם מחיצות, מביא:
Rashi on Shabbat 150b:9:3.english: Rather, what are the needs of a corpse - [It refers to] bringing a coffin and shrouds. And why [is it] not [permitted] for another [person]? Let us say [that] since if there were partitions there, one may bring [them].

Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:11:1.hebrew: אבל מחשיך הוא לשמור ומביא פירות בידו - מתוך פירוש הקונטרס משמע: לשמור חוץ לתחום, וכן משמע פשט המשנה. וקשה לרבי מהא דאמר שמואל בגמ': "מותר לאדם לומר לחבירו: לכרך פלוני אני הולך למחר", ופריך: "תנן אין מחשיכין על התחום לשכור פועלים כו'". והשתא מתניתין גופיה תיקשי ליה, דמוכחא מילתא כוותיה דשמואל, מדקתני בסיפא: "כלל אמר אבא שאול: כל שאני זכאי באמירתו — יכול אני להחשיך עליו", וקא מפרש בגמ' דמה שמותר לומר — מותר להחשיך; וא"כ, מדשרינן להחשיך לשמור חוץ לתחום, אלמא שרי למימר "חוץ לתחום אני הולך למחר", דהא בהא תליא, והיינו כשמואל. ואיני יודע מאי קשיא, דאי לאו דשמואל, מתני' אתיא שפיר, דה"א אין לך דבר שלא יהא מותר לאדם לומר על עצמו, ואפי' "אשכור פועלים למחר" או "אבנה בנין זה" יכול לומר בשבת, דהוה אמינא דווקא לחבירו אסור לומר "שכור לי פועלים למחר", דמהני אמירתו, אבל על עצמו יכול לומר כל מה שירצה, דלא מהני אמירתו. וכי תלי אבא שאול ההחשכה, ה"מ באמירה לחבירו, דיש אסורה ויש מותרת. אבל אם איתא לדשמואל, פריך שפיר, דאסר כל אמירות אפילו על עצמו, אלא דווקא "לכרך פלוני אני הולך למחר", משום טעמא דשאם יש שם בורגנין הולך. והשתא פריך: כיון דאי לאו האי טעמא הוה אסרת ליה, אלא משום האי טעמא דווקא שרית ליה, א"כ מתני' נמי תשתרי להביא פירות, שאם יש מחיצות מביא. נ"ל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:11:1.english: But he may wait for nightfall to guard [them] and bring produce in his hand - From the commentary of Rashi it is implied [that this means] to guard [them] outside the [Shabbat] boundary, and so too the plain sense of the Mishnah implies. And it is difficult for the Rabbi from that which Shmuel said in the Gemara: "It is permitted for a person to say to his fellow, 'To such-and-such a city I am going tomorrow,'" and [the Gemara] asks: "We learned [in the Mishnah]: One may not wait for nightfall at the boundary to hire workers, etc." Now, our Mishnah itself should pose a difficulty for him [the questioner], for the matter is proven in accordance with Shmuel, from what [the Mishnah] teaches in the latter clause: "Abba Shaul stated a general rule: Whatever I am entitled to say [on Shabbat], I may wait for nightfall for it," and [the Gemara] explains that whatever is permitted to say is permitted to wait for at nightfall. And if so, since we permit waiting for nightfall to guard outside the boundary, it follows that it is permitted to say, "I am going outside the boundary tomorrow," for one depends on the other — and this is like Shmuel! And I do not know what the difficulty is: for if not for Shmuel's [statement], the Mishnah would work out well, as I would have thought that there is nothing a person is not permitted to say regarding himself, and even "I will hire workers tomorrow" or "I will build this building" one may say on Shabbat — for I would have thought that specifically to one's fellow is it forbidden to say, "Hire workers for me tomorrow," because his speech is effective, whereas regarding himself he may say whatever he wishes, since his speech is not effective. And when Abba Shaul made waiting for nightfall dependent [on speech], that applies to speaking to one's fellow, where some [speech] is forbidden and some is permitted. However, if Shmuel's [statement] is true, [the Gemara] asks well, for [Shmuel] forbids all [weekday] speech even regarding oneself, except specifically "To such-and-such a city I am going tomorrow," because of the reason that if there are burganin [shelters] there, he may go [on Shabbat]. And now [the Gemara] asks: Since if not for this reason you would have forbidden it to him, and you only permitted it to him because of this specific reason, if so, in our Mishnah too it should be permitted to bring produce, [on the grounds] that if there are enclosures, one may bring [them]! So it appears to me.

Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:5:1.hebrew: לכרך פלוני אני הולך - תימה, מאי איריא הוא? אפילו לחבירו נמי יכול לומר: "לך לי לכרך פלוני למחר", מהאי טעמא דקאמר. מדשרי שמואל לקמן לומר לחבירו "שמור לי פירות שבתחומך" אפילו בשבת, כ"ש שיכול לומר "שמור לי למחר". ואין לפרש דשאני התם שהן בתחומו, אבל אין יכול לומר לחבירו "שמור לי פירות שחוץ לתחומך", דנראה הוא שאפילו זה יכול לומר, מכיון שמותר להחשיך. וצ"ל דלא נקט שמואל דוקא "לכרך פלוני אני הולך", דהוא הדין לחבירו יכול לומר: "לך לי לכרך פלוני למחר":
Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:5:1.english: I am going to such and such city - This is puzzling: why did [the Gemara] specify himself? Even to his fellow as well he can say, "Go for me to such and such city tomorrow," for that [same] reason that [the Gemara] states. Since Shmuel permits later [on] saying to one's fellow, "Guard for me produce that is within your [Shabbat] boundary," even on Shabbat [itself], all the more so can he say, "Guard [it] for me tomorrow." And one should not explain that it is different there because it is within his [the fellow's] boundary, whereas one cannot say to his fellow, "Guard for me produce that is outside your boundary" — for it is apparent that even this he can say, since it is permitted to wait until dark [at the boundary]. And one must say that Shmuel did not state "I am going to such and such city" specifically, for the same law applies to his fellow — he can say [to him], "Go for me to such and such city tomorrow":

Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:7:1.hebrew: בשלמא קש במחובר משכחת לה - ה"נ הו"מ למימר מטעם מוקצה, דהא אינו ראוי למאכל בהמה, כדאמר לעיל (שבת דף קמא): "הקש שע"ג המטה לא ינענענו כו'"; אלא רבותא קאמר, דאפילו במחובר משכחת לה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:7:1.english: Granted, straw — you find it attached - Here too [the Gemara] could have said [that it is prohibited] on account of muktzeh, for it is not fit for animal food, as it says earlier (Shabbat 141a): "One may not move the straw that is on top of the bed, etc."; rather, it states a stronger point — that even [when it is] attached [to the ground] you find it:

Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:7:2.hebrew: במחובר משכחת לה - אומר רבי דלאו משום תלישה נקט לה, דאע"ג שמחובר לארץ, אין בו איסור תלישה; כיון שיבש, אינו יונק מן הארץ. כדמוכח בחולין פרק העור והרוטב (חולין דף קכז: ושם), דאמר: "תאנים שצמקו באביהן מטמאין טומאת אוכלין, והתולש ממנה בשבת חייב חטאת" — דווקא צמקו, אבל יבשו לא. וכן משמע בכל הסוגיא דיבשו הן ועוקציהן מטמא טומאת אוכלין, ואין דינו כלל כמחובר. והא דקאמר הכא "במחובר משכחת לה", היינו משום איסור ייפוי קרקע, כדאמר לעיל: "התולש עולשין בשבת חייב חטאת", בפרק הבונה (לעיל שבת דף קג.). והא דפריך בפרק המוציא תפילין (עירובין דף ק:) אאילן יבש: "הא קא נתרי פירי", משמע שיש ביבש איסור תלישה — אומר רבי דמיירי התם ביבשו הן ולא עוקציהן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:7:2.english: You find it [in the case of] attached [straw] - The Rabbi says that [the Gemara] did not mention it because of [the prohibition of] detaching, for even though it is attached to the ground, there is no prohibition of detaching with it; since it has dried out, it does not draw nourishment from the ground. As is proven in Chullin, chapter Ha'or Veharotav (Chullin 127b, and there [in the parallel]), where it states: "Figs that shriveled while still attached to their stems are susceptible to food impurity, and one who detaches from it on Shabbat is liable for a sin-offering" — specifically [when] they shriveled, but [if] they dried out [completely], [he is] not [liable]. And so it is implied throughout the entire sugya, that [when] both they and their stems dried out, it is susceptible to food impurity, and its status is not at all like [something] attached. And that which it says here, "You find it [in the case of] attached [straw]," is because of the prohibition of improving the land, as it says earlier: "One who detaches endives on Shabbat is liable for a sin-offering," in chapter HaBoneh (earlier, Shabbat 103a). And [as for] that which it asks in chapter HaMotzi Tefillin (Eruvin 100b) regarding a dry tree: "But fruits are falling off!" — [which] implies that there is a prohibition of detaching with [something] dry — the Rabbi says that there it is dealing with [a case] where they [the fruits] dried out, but not their stems.

Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:7:3.hebrew: בתיבנא סריא - והא דאמר לקמן פרק מי שהחשיך (שבת דף קנה:): "מפרכין תבן ואספסתא לפני בהמה", ומוקי לה בתבנא סריא, משמע דחזי לבהמה — אומר רבי דמיירי כגון דלא סרי' כולי האי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:7:3.english: To rotten straw - And [as for] that which it says later in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehechshikh (Shabbat 155b): "One may crumble straw and alfalfa before an animal," and [the Gemara there] establishes it [as referring] to rotten straw, which implies that it is fit for an animal — the Rabbi says that [there] it is speaking of a case where it is not rotten to such an extent.

Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:9:1.hebrew: אלא מת מאי ניהו להביא לו ארון ותכריכין - תימה: אמאי לא קאמר "למיגז ליה אסא", שהיו רגילין להביא אסא למת, כדאשכחן בנדה (דף לז.) דשוור אסא מערסא לערסא? וי"ל: ע"כ צ"ל "ארון ותכריכין", כדקתני במתני' בהדיא. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150b:9:1.english: "But [with regard to] a corpse, what is it? To bring for it a coffin and shrouds" - It is surprising: why does [the Gemara] not say "to cut a myrtle [branch] for it," since they were accustomed to bring myrtle for a corpse, as we find in Niddah (37a), where a myrtle [branch] leaped from bier to bier? And one can say [in answer]: perforce [the Gemara] must say "a coffin and shrouds," as is taught explicitly in the Mishnah. [From my teacher.]
